answer: The defence rests on insurance premium streak with policy renewals: a policy renewed every year with the same insurer. Forging 413 of these means building 413 separate premium streaks from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. Call it the vine rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the lantern record is open for audit, and the terrace window is too short for 413 aliases to earn their price back.
